changes.title: Edits that no change claims are attached to the change that has the most pieces in their module, shown as "also changed with it", instead of all landing in Other edits.

how.words: The prompt now asks the AI to put every piece into a change rather than leaving unclaimed ones out, so fewer pieces are left over.

New helpers `docair-core.review.attach_by_module`, `docair-core.review.modules_of` and `docair-core.review.parent_id` score each leftover piece by the modules it shares with a change's pieces and attach it to the clear winner; `docair-ai.explain.comment` and `docair-viewer.page_changes.review_view` both call it and list the attached pieces under their change.
Wires the review-comment builder into the change's piece list so the attached pieces can be shown there too.

changes.why: Too many edits were left as unexplained "other edits" (32 on the last run); a rule docair can stand behind attaches them by where the code sits, since the model groups by meaning and this only by location.
changes.check: Check that a piece is only attached when one change clearly has more pieces in the piece's module — ties and zero-overlap pieces must stay in Other edits, or unrelated edits get explained under the wrong change.

changes.title: The changes panel shows the flows right after the review, with how many of the system's flows changed, and the other edits come last, folded.

how.words: The changes view now counts all of the system's flows via `docair-core.slice.all` to report "n of the system's m" next to the changed flows.
Feeds the flow titles from the full slice set so the flow list can be headed with the system-wide count.
The end-to-end test now checks the flows head comes right after the changes with a count of the system's flows, and that the other-edits box sits last and is closed (folded).

changes.why: The flows the review is built from were not visible where a reader looks, and the reader had no sense of how much of the system they cover; the other edits were moved to the end and folded to keep the review first.
changes.check: Check the system-wide flow count excludes part-seeded slices correctly, so the "n of m" figure is not inflated or deflated.

changes.title: A review change opens on "What and why" — what was done, why, what to check and where it disagrees — before walking through its pieces as "How · k of n".

how.words: The review view gains an `other` field so the other edits render folded after the flows, and the walk flag passed for flow pictures changes from `false` to `None` so only review changes carry the intro framing.
The change walk now calls docair-core.review.cut to trim the change's title to a heading for the new first card.
The walk builds an extra first step card ("What and why") with its own navigation, so the pieces follow as "How · k of n".
The end-to-end test now checks the review opens on "What and why" showing the change's title and why, then the how step with the model's words.

changes.why: The walk previously jumped straight into the pieces; the commit and docs want each change to open on its title with what, why, what to check and disagreements framed on the whole change, then the how steps.
changes.check: Check the intro card is only added to review-change walks and not to per-flow pictures, and that the "How · k of n" numbering still matches the piece order.
